label: Data rate per tree
info:
Counts messages and bytes per tree on the broker: the customer tree (v1.0/DRWPA/…) and the CH tree per asset serial (v1.0/CH/Fleet/…/<serial>/…), split into process values and raw waveform blocks.

Every 10 s the node status and the debug sidebar show messages/s and KB/s. This is the load an edge device on this broker has to take, and what would leave the site if everything were sent.

label: Bearing pads → 1-min CSV
info:
Subscribes to the CH tree only and writes one row per asset per minute to `exports/ch_bearings_1min.csv` (host folder): the operating context (MW, net head, cooling water inlet temperature and flow) next to the TGB pad and oil temperatures and the hottest thrust pad.

These are the inputs of a level 3 residual model (pad temperature expected from MW, cooling water and oil temperature vs. measured), the flagship demo for scenario A. Values with a quality other than GOOD are left out of the averages. The file is set by `BEARING_CSV_FILE`.

label: Draft tube block → dominant frequency (example)
info:
**An example of edge analytics, not part of the CH PLC.** The PLC only publishes raw blocks. This flow takes each 10 s draft-tube pressure block (100 S/s), removes the mean and runs a plain DFT over 0.2–10 Hz. The dominant frequency and amplitude show the vortex rope (0.2–0.4 × the 5 Hz runner frequency) when a unit runs at part load, e.g. in instructor scenario C.

Real edge analytics (FFT, orbits, envelope, order tracking, models) is what the edge vendors bring.
